issue.title: test_empty_panel_escape_follows_the_hide_panel_binding flakes under parallel check, passes in isolation
issue.description:
Proposed by phase sase-1eq.1.1.7 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #2) and triaged by the sase-1eq.1.1 land agent. Not caused by epic sase-1eq.1.1: the epic changed only sase-core, and this ACE command-line test does not consume the directive or macro catalog surfaces it changed.

The test opens the command-line panel with `hide_panel` rebound to `f8`, then presses Escape inside `asyncio.wait_for(page.press("escape"), timeout=1.0)`. The likely cause is the fixed 1-second pilot-press budget, which a loaded parallel pytest lane can exceed. That is not proven yet; investigate before changing anything. Never weaken the assertion. Adjacent family: sase-1al (a different node in `test_panel_shell.py` with the same parallel-lane-only failure pattern).

task_type_fields.evidence: Failed in sase check ToolRun be10642d5e6eb75dc01985981dba118c (scoped lane with 7 workers, 51601 passed and 5 failed, run for sase-1eq.1.1.7). Triage marked it KNOWN with witness ToolRun 113a355046bd2d7071046552723af448 (sase-1es.3 landing check). Phase 7 reported KNOWN witnesses from 6 agents and 6 workspaces. On 2026-10-02 the land agent ran it in isolation (`pytest tests/ace/tui/command_line/test_panel_shell_pilot.py::test_empty_panel_escape_follows_the_hide_panel_binding`) on sase acac8d83e0..e34386fee4: it passed. It fails only under parallel load and passes serially.
